headline: arXivLabs: Collaborators Develop New arXiv Features on Website
summary: arXiv introduces arXivLabs, a framework for external collaborators to build and share new features directly on the arXiv website, emphasizing openness and user privacy.
details: arXiv has launched arXivLabs, a new framework designed to foster collaboration and innovation on its platform. This initiative allows external individuals and organizations to develop and deploy new features directly on the arXiv website.

The program is built upon arXiv's core values of openness, community engagement, excellence, and a strong commitment to user data privacy. arXiv states that it exclusively partners with entities that uphold these principles.

arXivLabs aims to empower its community by providing a structured environment for developing and testing new functionalities. This could range from improved search capabilities to novel ways of interacting with research papers.
Interested parties with ideas for projects that could enhance the arXiv experience are encouraged to learn more about the arXivLabs program and its submission process.

headline: PaperPilot – Pure-Rust PDF engine for AI agents, runs locally
summary: This new open-source toolkit written in Rust offers a zero-cloud PDF engine that processes documents entirely on your machine, enhancing privacy and security for AI agent workflows.
details: PaperPilot is a new PDF and document toolkit developed entirely in Rust, designed to run locally without uploading any files to the cloud. This makes it ideal for AI agents and users concerned about data privacy and security.

The engine offers a wide range of functionalities, including organizing documents by merging, splitting, rotating, and reordering pages. It also supports page extraction, booklet imposition, and N-up grid layouts.
For optimization, PaperPilot can compress PDFs and extract plain text. It also includes OCR capabilities powered by a pure-Rust implementation of PaddleOCR via rten.

Security features are robust, with options for watermarking, signature validation, signature removal, PII scanning, and deep sanitization of documents. These features ensure sensitive information remains protected.

Beyond PDF manipulation, PaperPilot can also process Office documents, converting Excel files to JSON or CSV formats. An Enterprise Edition with advanced features like SSO and RBAC is also in development.

The project is open-source under the Apache 2.0 license, including the CLI, MCP server, REST gateway, WASM engine, and desktop app. Developers are encouraged to contribute bug reports, tool requests, and documentation fixes.
